scene.renderer: three.js r170, WebGL, transparent canvas (.spores), antialias, low-power, pixel ratio max 2, ACES filmic tone mapping (exposure 1 light / .9 dark), sRGB output; lazy-loaded, optional; removed if WebGL or the import fails
scene.placement: absolute canvas around the hero h1, tabs, intro and "more about me" bounds plus 120px padding (clamped to the viewport width), under the text; radial ellipse mask 58% x 34%: solid to 42%, .82 at 58%, .30 at 74%, transparent at 100%
scene.field: one particle per 2400px2 of canvas, 60 to 420; ~14% chrome beads; one world unit = one CSS pixel on the text plane; PerspectiveCamera fov 32
scene.dots: InstancedMesh spheres, radius 1-1.9px, MeshStandardMaterial roughness .7 metalness 0, colour = live --soft
scene.beads: InstancedMesh spheres, radius 2.8-5.6px, MeshStandardMaterial metalness 1 roughness .08; white + envMapIntensity 1.25 in dark, gunmetal #5d6068 + envMapIntensity 1.6 on light paper
scene.lighting: RoomEnvironment via PMREM (.03), environment intensity 1 light / .7 dark; one directional key light 1.2 from (-1, 1.4, 1.2)
scene.depth: z from -320px (behind) to 160px (in front of) the text plane
scene.pauses: render loop stops off screen (IntersectionObserver) and in hidden tabs; reduced motion draws one static frame and redraws only on theme change
scene.thinning: particles near the .for-intro box thin out (smoothstep on distance): dots to 30% within 28px, chrome beads to 0 within 44px

narrative.northStar: A Quiet Desk with Dust in the Light
narrative.overview:
Etharic is one calm reading system: cool paper, graphite ink, hairline borders, Inter at reading sizes and flat surfaces on every route. The homepage keeps that desk and lets a little air move over it. A left-aligned column says "hey, i'm suryanarayan!", lets the visitor pick who they are from a row of plain text tabs, and answers in a large intro paragraph written for that reader. Behind the greeting a sparse field of tiny particles drifts in real 3D, most of them matte grey dots in the page's own soft tone and a few small chrome beads that catch the light. It is atmosphere, not an object: no frame, no colour, fading out at its edges.

The first screen is the greeting alone, closed by one bottom row on the 24px gutter: the "currently in" line with its clock, green dot and pixel dog on the left, a soft "picked for <audience> ↓" cue in the centre that scrolls to the picks, and "get cv" in burnt amber on the right. Below the fold, "picked for <audience>" lists three hand-picked pieces of writing that follow the selected tab, then closes with "all essays → · get cv · say hi".

The voice is personal and playful (lowercase copy, code-like terms such as `this.essay` set in a mono face, a pixel dog, a live clock) while the surfaces stay restrained. Rejected: corporate polish, glossy neon 3D, glass, decorative gradients and glow halos.
keyCharacteristics: Flat tonal surfaces with 1px hairlines; no elevation shadows.
Graphite carries everything; burnt amber is the one action colour ("get cv"), signal green the one status colour.
Inter for everything, with JetBrains Mono only for the code-like terms inside homepage intros.
The audience choice changes words, not colours: the intro text and the picked cards swap, nothing is recoloured.
The particle field is the one rendered effect: grey and chrome, slow, behind the text, paused when unseen, static under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Words-Not-Colours Rule
rules.body: Choosing an audience changes what the page says, never its palette. Tabs, intro and cards stay in graphite and soft graphite for every reader.

rules.name: The One Warm Thing Rule
rules.body: Burnt amber marks the single action a visitor might take from anywhere on the first screen ("get cv"). Nothing decorative is amber.

rules.name: The Mono Aside Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for code-like terms inside running intro text. It never sets a heading, a control or a whole sentence.

rules.name: The Steady Width Rule
rules.body: A tab that turns bold must not push its neighbours: each tab reserves its bold width in advance, and the intro reserves the height of its longest text, so switching audiences never shifts the page.

rules.name: The Material Depth Rule
rules.body: If something looks raised, it is because it is rendered in 3D or has a lighter tone, not because it casts a box-shadow.

rules.name: The Atmosphere Rule
rules.body: The particles stay behind the text, small, grey or chrome, thinned behind the intro and masked at their edges. They never take an accent colour, never sit in front of a control, and the page reads fully without them.

dos: Do take every colour from the tokens, with a dark value for each page surface.
Do keep the homepage first screen to the greeting, the tabs, the intro and "more about me", closed by the one bottom row: "currently in" left, the picked-for cue centred, "get cv" right.
Do let the audience choice change words and picks, and keep the page's colours the same for every reader.
Do reserve space for the longest intro and the bold tab width so switching audiences never shifts the layout.
Do keep the particle field behind the text, masked at its edges, paused off screen and in hidden tabs, and static under reduced motion.
Do animate only transform, opacity and filter with `--ease-out` (`cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)`), 160 to 300ms; keep an opacity-only fallback under reduced motion.
Do keep a 2px graphite ink focus ring on every control, a 44px tap area on every homepage tab and link, and full keyboard operation of the tabs.
donts: Don't use box-shadows, glass, glow halos or decorative gradients to suggest depth.
Don't colour the particles or add a second rendered 3D effect.
Don't use burnt amber for decoration or signal green for anything but status.
Don't set headings, tabs or whole sentences in JetBrains Mono.
